# Unit rules

The unit files are parsed with systemd's rules (sections, `Key=value`, `\` continuations; list settings such as `After=`, `Environment=` and `ExecStart=` of oneshot services accumulate and an empty assignment resets them) and checked against the following. An unknown section or key, a misspelled boolean or a relative program path is an error.

1. **`atlas.service`**: `Type=simple`; exactly one `ExecStart=` unless the type is `oneshot`; the program of every `ExecStart=` is an absolute path; effective `ExecStart=` (in this order): `/opt/atlas/bin/atlas serve --config /etc/atlas/atlas.toml`; `ExecReload=`: `/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID`; `User=atlas`; `Restart=on-failure` and `RestartSec=` a time span between 1 s and 60 s (`5`, `5s`, `1min 30s` are all fine); `After=` is exactly {network-online.target, postgresql.service, redis.service}; `Requires=` is exactly {postgresql.service}; `Wants=` is exactly {redis.service, network-online.target}; every unit named in `After=`/`Before=`/`Requires=`/`Wants=` exists in the project or on the system (known system units: `network.target`, `network-online.target`, `multi-user.target`, `timers.target`, `sockets.target`, `postgresql.service`, `redis.service`, `nginx.service`, `docker.service`, `local-fs.target`, `remote-fs.target`); `Requires=X` also needs `After=X`; `Wants=network-online.target` only works with `After=network-online.target`; `[Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target`; `NoNewPrivileges=yes`; `PrivateTmp=yes`; `ProtectSystem=` is one of `strict`; `ProtectHome=` is one of `yes`, `true`; `CapabilityBoundingSet=` is empty (drops every capability); with `ProtectSystem=strict` the file system is read-only except `ReadWritePaths=` and the managed directories (`StateDirectory=x` is `/var/lib/x`, `LogsDirectory=x` is `/var/log/x`, `CacheDirectory=x` is `/var/cache/x`); the service writes to `/var/lib/atlas`, `/var/log/atlas`; `Environment=` sets `ATLAS_ENV=production`; `Environment=` sets `ATLAS_WORKERS=8`; `EnvironmentFile=` is `-/etc/atlas/atlas.env`; `LimitNOFILE=65536`.
2. **`atlas-cleanup.service`**: `Type=oneshot`; every `ExecStart=` program is an absolute path; effective `ExecStart=` (in this order): `/opt/atlas/bin/atlas cleanup --older-than 30d`; `User=atlas`; every unit named in `After=`/`Before=`/`Requires=`/`Wants=` exists in the project or on the system (known system units: `network.target`, `network-online.target`, `multi-user.target`, `timers.target`, `sockets.target`, `postgresql.service`, `redis.service`, `nginx.service`, `docker.service`, `local-fs.target`, `remote-fs.target`); `Requires=X` also needs `After=X`; `Wants=network-online.target` only works with `After=network-online.target`; no `[Install] WantedBy=` (another unit starts it).
3. **`atlas-cleanup.timer`**: `OnCalendar=` fires at exactly the same moments as the intended schedule (the checker compares the firing minutes over several weeks; this is not cron: a weekday list is `Mon..Fri`, `Sat,Sun`; the day-of-week and the date must both match); `Persistent=yes`; `RandomizedDelaySec=1800` seconds; the unit it activates (`Unit=`, or the service of the same name) is one of the project's units; `[Install] WantedBy=timers.target`.

prompt: Write the units of the `atlas` application. `atlas.service`: `/opt/atlas/bin/atlas serve --config /etc/atlas/atlas.toml`, user `atlas`, `ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID`, environment `ATLAS_ENV=production` and `ATLAS_WORKERS=8`, optional environment file `/etc/atlas/atlas.env` (the leading `-` makes a missing file fine), restart on failure after 10 s, `LimitNOFILE=65536`; ordering: after `network-online.target`, `postgresql.service` and `redis.service`, requires PostgreSQL, wants Redis and the online network; hardening: `NoNewPrivileges`, `PrivateTmp`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome=yes`, state in `/var/lib/atlas` and logs in `/var/log/atlas` (managed directories), no capabilities; enabled in multi-user boot. `atlas-cleanup.service`: a one-shot (`/opt/atlas/bin/atlas cleanup --older-than 30d`, user `atlas`, no `[Install]`) and `atlas-cleanup.timer`: every Sunday at 03:15, persistent, randomized delay up to 30 minutes (1800 s), enabled with the timers target. `UNIT_RULES.md` lists what the unit files are checked against.
